newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures close up as bonds help.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures close up as bonds help.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures finished an abbreviated session mostly firmer as strong bond prices spilled over into equities, traders said.
"It's no great shakes. Bonds are looking pretty good today," said one S&P 500 index futures trader.
Some light short-covering by locals also helped strengthen the December S&P 500 index futures contract, which settled at 758.25, up 2.30.
Traders said the December contract got stuck at a resistance band that runs from 760.50 to 761.50. The contract's intraday peak was 760.70, reached off the opening.

"We were having trouble sustaining anything above the 760-even level," said one S&P 500 index futures trader said. He added that even so, sentiment remained firm ahead of the key November U.S. jobless report, due December 6.
One index options trader characterized the market's strength as resulting more from an absence of sellers than from an influx of buyers.
"You got a good spike up early, but volume dropped off considerably," one trader said.
December Nasdaq 100 index futures rose 3.90 to 837.50, off their 840 session peak.
December Value Line index futures on the Kansas City Board of Trade rose 0.80 to 683 and December Russell 2000 index futures gained 0.60 to 355.35.
Nikkei 225 stock index futures bucked the trend, with the December contract dropping 230 to 21,105.
Traders said investors were beginning to roll positions into March contracts, particularly in S&Ps, where the December expires in three weeks.
The spread between December and March S&Ps narrowed to about seven points from 7.20 points Wednesday.
Based on fair value, the premium between the two contracts should be about 6.50 points. At the beginning of November, the spread stood at 6.25 points, one floor analyst said.
